value: **Direct Callouts & Context**: "Research shows that compared to a free setting and a highly structured setting, children’s active participation in discovery, combined with appropriate scaffolding from a knowledgeable adult, a higher level of engagement and better learning result (Sim & Xu, 2015)." | "The educational principles underpinning this design, such as collaborative play and scaffolding, are rooted in general education practices, suggesting their adaptability across various neurotypes and learning contexts." | "Future work should explore how emotional transitions can be used in real-time to guide adaptive scaffolding, particularly in collaborative settings where affective states are influenced by both individual and peer dynamics."
